title: Regional energy-cost differences remain important to sourcing
global_view: Gas and electricity exposures vary by region and contract; overseas energy-intensive suppliers need local assessment.
us_view: Lower average wholesale energy prices may coexist with rising local network, demand or capacity costs.
procurement_actions: Map facility tariffs, load and pass-throughs
Stage purchases within approved limits; test regional supplier exposure
review_triggers: New EIA outlook or regional tariff
counterevidence: Benign weather, improved fuel supply or lower network costs could reduce pressure.

evaluation.criterion: Review delivered-cost evidence by region; do not score a universal price direction or exact site savings.

title: Connection and execution constraints remain uneven
global_view: Shared equipment and engineering supply can transmit demand internationally; U.S. queue statistics do not measure global delays.
us_view: Obtain facility-specific utility and manufacturing milestones; generation queues do not measure load connection waits.
procurement_actions: Verify energization and factory slots before capital approval
Qualify alternate equipment and approved repair sources
review_triggers: New queue study or dated qualified quote
counterevidence: Faster reforms, withdrawn projects and new qualified output could ease selected bottlenecks.

evaluation.criterion: Compare new connection and equipment evidence while preserving population and duration definitions; require site proof before an investment claim.

title: Renewable cost benefits depend on location and delivery
global_view: Project financing, resources and installation costs can offset cheap hardware.
us_view: Landed costs, trade remedies, labor, tax eligibility and commissioning determine buyer economics.
procurement_actions: Compare commissioned lifecycle cost and no-credit case
Allocate EPC and equipment interfaces and origin liability
review_triggers: New trade order or interconnection event
counterevidence: More qualified supply, cheaper finance and faster connections could improve savings.

evaluation.criterion: Reassess like-for-like bids and comparable cost studies; do not substitute global LCOE for U.S. tariffs.

title: Storage growth creates opportunities with contract and integration risk
global_view: Deployment forecasts broaden beyond the largest markets, but a forecast is not capacity already shipping.
us_view: Usable MW/MWh, dispatch rights, throughput, warranties and eligible supply matter more than pack price alone.
procurement_actions: Tender usable performance, augmentation and service
Verify supply acceptance obligations and credit documentation
review_triggers: Changed market rights, cycles or warranties
counterevidence: Factory delays, weaker economics or policy changes could reduce deployment; competition may improve hardware bids.

evaluation.criterion: Review newer deployment evidence and actual project performance; do not score full-year 2027 totals before data are available.

title: Processing and license exposure persist despite better aggregate supply outlooks
global_view: Refining concentration and restrictions can constrain access despite sufficient global capacity.
us_view: Map processors and component inputs; two assemblers may share the same upstream source.
procurement_actions: Use selective buffers and transparent material-index clauses
review_triggers: Evidence on suspension extension or new capacity
counterevidence: New refining capacity, substitutions or eased controls could improve access.

evaluation.criterion: Compare access, concentration and short-term supply evidence; keep post-2027 deficits as context.

title: Fuel-logistics normalization remains uncertain
global_view: Product availability and route/insurance stress can outlast restored crude flows.
us_view: Diesel-sensitive operations need transparent surcharges, alternative terminals and continuity plans.
procurement_actions: Separate crude, product basis and freight risks
Audit surcharge resets and alternate supply
counterevidence: Sustained route reopening and inventory rebuilding could ease costs sooner.

evaluation.criterion: Monitor product inventories and route-specific freight; timing confidence remains low and no fixed normalization date is claimed.

title: U.S. gas supply may buffer export growth, with local risks
global_view: LNG importers face a different shipping and contract mix from U.S. Henry Hub buyers.
us_view: Production/inventory growth may offset LNG demand, but weather and pipeline basis can dominate a facility bill.
procurement_actions: Quote delivered basis and firm transport separately
Review interruptible service and backup fuel
counterevidence: Production shortfalls or prolonged cold would weaken the buffer; lower demand could strengthen it.

evaluation.criterion: Compare EIA forecast revisions and realized gas balances; retain full-year 2027 as context outside the exact report horizon.

title: Trade and eligibility rules continue to segment sourcing
global_view: Diversification can redirect trade without removing origin, refining or remedy exposure.
us_view: Recheck product scope, producer, HTS/Chapter 99 codes, entry date and credit assumptions before purchase.
procurement_actions: Obtain current broker/legal treatment and supplier certifications
Contract for duties, customs delays and change-in-law allocation
review_triggers: New order, CBP instruction or HTS change
New IRS guidance or ownership/origin change
counterevidence: Stable rules or valid exclusions may reduce costs; legal status may change in either direction.

evaluation.criterion: Reverify operative documents every update and before transactions; do not predict an exact future tariff rate or legal outcome.
